author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: I need to be clear about the validation process. We are keeping the current manual checks in place for the time being. The infrastructure costs required to build an automated layer right now are simply too high for our budget. I will not approve the move to automation until we have a much cheaper path. The manual process is sufficient to manage the risk we face today. Please treat this as a hard line. Any proposal that ignores this cost constraint will be rejected by me. We cannot spend money we do not have just to fix a problem that our current team handles without major incident.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly defines a cost constraint as a 'hard line' and states that any proposal ignoring it will be rejected, indicating a refusal threshold rather than a preference for more automation.
